slides.title: Hybi's downhill prep routine
slides.sub: Start a few weeks before the hike!

sections.heading: 1. Train the brakes at home
lines: ① Slow step-downs from a low step, 10 reps.
② Split squats, 8 reps each leg.
④ 2–3 times a week, build over weeks.

sections.heading: 2. Stop and get advice if…
lines: The knee swells, locks or gives way,
or pain lasts for days after a hike.

slides.heading: Get it checked if you notice

caption:
Legs fine on the way up, knees complaining on the way down? Descents are often the harder part.

Going downhill, your thigh muscles work as brakes while they lengthen, which loads the front of the knee more than climbing. Tired legs late in a hike make it harder still.

Shorter steps, a slight knee bend, zigzagging down steep sections and walking poles can all help share the load. At home, slow step-downs, split squats and wall sits can help build capacity over a few weeks.

Swelling, locking, giving way or pain that lasts for days after a hike is worth an assessment. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help you plan your next trail. Book online via the link in bio.
